title: Cereal losses at harvest, on-farm storage and collection are linked to poorly set harvesting machinery, an old farm machinery stock and open-air storage, but have been measured only once, in two governorates

rootCauses.cause: Harvest losses from poorly adjusted combine harvesters, within an old farm machinery stock (60% of all farm machines over 25 years old); small farmers depend on machinery owners and have little bargaining power
Collection centres short of capacity and modern equipment: open-air or uncovered bunker storage in big harvest years, fragile plastic sacks, manual handling, old concrete silos

Administered cereal chain: the Office des Céréales fixes prices and margins at every stage and the state bears most storage and logistics costs; the study says millers are not paid for storing grain and have weak incentives to invest, while weak incentives for collectors are an inference from this system
Poor coordination between farmers and collection centres, little contracting, and a parallel informal circuit for grain

dataGaps: The FAO/ministry phase 2 report that measured cereal losses in Bizerte and Siliana (2017-2018) was not found online; its figures reach us only through two press articles that disagree (4.6-7.3% vs 3.6-5.4%).

No national cereal loss estimate: FAO Food Loss Index (SDG 12.3.1a) has no value for Tunisia (SRC-TG-900); FAOSTAT food balance 'losses' for wheat could not be retrieved (the API now requires authorisation).
Whether the ministry actually added loss measurement to its annual agricultural surveys, as planned (SRC-TG-904).
Storage losses in Office des Céréales silos and in big harvest years when open-air storage is used: no figures found.

Fruit and vegetable post-harvest losses (wholesale markets, cold chain): only a 1999 CIHEAM paper on the Bir El Kassaa market turned up, and its host (ressources.ciheam.org) did not resolve; no recent Tunisian measurement found.
A sourced projection of future grain losses: the only climate study found (SRC-TG-905) models pest dynamics and aeration feasibility, not losses.
author: TahaGHZ
excerpt: Part of Tunisia's cereal harvest is lost before it reaches mills, at harvest, in on-farm storage and at collection centres. Until the FAO/Italy project of 2016-2018 no chain-level estimate existed; the FAO evaluation…

sections.heading: Problem
sections.content: Part of Tunisia's cereal harvest is lost before it reaches mills, at harvest, in on-farm storage and at collection centres. Until the FAO/Italy project of 2016-2018 no chain-level estimate existed; the FAO evaluation calls that project's work the first-ever estimate of losses in the cereal and milk chains (SRC-TG-904), and the project's own diagnostic said in 2017 that few data exist on the scale of losses at each stage (SRC-TG-901). The one measurement, in Bizerte and Siliana, reached the public only through press. One article gives average farm-level losses of 4.6% in Bizerte to 7.3% in Siliana and collection losses of 0.38% and 0.24% (SRC-TG-908); another gives post-harvest losses of 3.6% to 5.4% for the same governorates (SRC-TG-909). The losses were estimated to cost each cereal farmer 832 TND a year in Bizerte and 578 TND in Siliana (SRC-TG-908). In a country that depends heavily on cereal imports (FND-TG-700), a loss of a few percent of a harvest that already swings with rainfall (FND-TG-701) matters for import needs, but its national size is unknown.

sections.heading: Root causes
sections.content:
- **Harvest machinery.** The FAO/ministry diagnostic says mechanical harvesting in Tunisia is "réputée pour les importantes pertes qu'elle occasionne". It cites the ministry for 60% of all farm machines being over 25 years old, which "occasionne une perte de 100 millions de dinars par an" (SRC-TG-901); the figure covers all farm machinery and the nature of the loss is not stated, so it is not a grain-loss estimate. Its example of 10% harvest losses (1.7 million quintals on a 17 million quintal harvest) is a hypothetical illustration, not a measurement (SRC-TG-901). Small farmers depend on combine owners and have little bargaining power over the service (SRC-TG-901).
- **On-farm storage.** Farmers who store grain to sell gradually are not trained in storage practice. The gap between harvest and collection (collection is 40-50% of the harvest) is usually counted as self-consumption, seed and feed, but probably contains losses that are hard to quantify (SRC-TG-901).
- **Collection centres.** The diagnostic lists manual handling, old or missing equipment, old concrete silos, frequent open-air storage or uncovered "Australian" bunker silos, fragile plastic sacks and, in good rainy years, extra open-air storage that exposes grain to birds, rodents, rain and theft (SRC-TG-901).
- **Institutional set-up (legacy decision).** The Office des Céréales fixes prices and margins at every stage, and the CGC covers its "sales at a loss", so most storage and logistics costs fall on the state (SRC-TG-901). Collection privatisation looks like sub-contracting rather than real privatisation, and the Office does not pay millers for storage, so they under-invest in silos (SRC-TG-901). The history of this system is in FND-TG-702.
- **Coordination.** In Bizerte and Siliana, the study notes weak contracting, small farms with little access to technical support, and a parallel circuit of intermediaries and informal trade (SRC-TG-901).

sections.heading: Evidence
sections.content:
See indicators. Measured rates exist only for two northern governorates and come from press summaries of the FAO/ministry phase 2 study (SRC-TG-908, SRC-TG-909). The two articles disagree; they may describe different scopes (farm stage only vs all post-harvest stages), but neither says so, so both values are recorded. The FAO "19%" for cereal losses and waste is a Near East and North Africa regional estimate, not a Tunisian one (SRC-TG-901).

**Future.** The only projection found concerns stored wheat in north-western Tunisia for 2041-2070 under RCP4.5 and RCP8.5. Hours suitable for cooling grain by ambient aeration fall by 25% on average, weakening a key pest-control method, but the modelled lesser grain borer (*Rhyzopertha dominica*) reproduces 20-30% less and survives 5-10% less than in 1970-1997 (SRC-TG-905). The study does not estimate losses and its results point in opposite directions, so it does not support a "predicted" finding that storage losses will rise. Only the abstract was read.

sections.heading: Why confidence is what it is
sections.content: Low. The causes rest on one FAO/ministry diagnostic (tier B) that itself says the losses were not yet measured. The only loss rates are tier C (press summaries of an unpublished or unfound report), cover two governorates and one season, and disagree with each other. There is no national figure from FAOSTAT or the SDG database. The 60% machinery age figure is second-hand (the diagnostic citing the ministry) and covers all farm machinery, not combines only.

sections.heading: Links to other sectors
sections.content:
- Water: none found.
- Energy: none found.
- Climate and drought: the size of the harvest, and so of open-air storage, varies with rainfall (FND-TG-701; SRC-TG-901); climate change reduces aeration hours for stored wheat (SRC-TG-905).

sections.heading: Leads for phase 2
sections.content:
- National action plans and loss-reduction charter for the cereal chain with the central wheat cooperative, FAO project GCP/RNE/004/ITA (SRC-TG-904)
- Planned integration of loss measurement into the ministry's annual agricultural surveys (SRC-TG-904)
- Investment code 2017 implementing decrees: up to 50% support for renewing farm machinery (SRC-TG-901)
- Ambient-air aeration and adaptive pest management for stored wheat (SRC-TG-905)
- World Bank-supported grain value chain reforms, including digital tracking of durum distribution (in FND-TG-702, SRC-TG-705)

resolvedSources.title: Project Paper on a proposed additional loan of US$300 million for a Second Additional Financing to the Tunisia Emergency Food Security Response Project (Report PAD5602)
resolvedSources.extracts:
Dated March 1, 2024. Sectoral context, para 8, p. 3:

> For the fourth consecutive year, below-average rainfall and extreme heat have combined to dramatically compromise Tunisia's grain production in 2022/23. As shown in Table 1 below, the Grain Board collected less than half of durum wheat quantities in 2023 compared to average drought years 2020-22 and two-thirds less than in a non-drought year (such as 2019), and almost no barley (1.3 percent of average drought years).

Table 1, "Grain quantities collected by OC (2019-2023)", '000 t, source Tunisia Grain Board (OC), rows (2019 / average 2020-2022 / 2023):

> Durum wheat 876.4 685.6 286.7
> Soft wheat 75.4 31.3 6.2
> Barley 332.9 39.5 0.5
> Total 1284.7 756.4 293.4

Para 8, p. 3 (continued):

> Consequently, average monthly grain import needs have skyrocketed (100,000 MT/month for durum wheat and 100,000 MT/month for barley, currently estimated at US$48 million/month for durum wheat and US$28 million/month for barley).

Footnote 15:

> This is particularly true in Tunisia where people remember vividly the bread riots that occurred from December 1983 to January 1984, triggered by a temporary rise in the price of bread due to the government austerity program.

Para 9, p. 3:

> For the period from July 2023 to June 2024, the Grain Board is facing an additional financing gap of around US$522 million due to very low local harvest of durum wheat and barley.

Footnote to Table 2, p. 4:

> Soft wheat import needs are not substantially impacted by drought since Tunisia is 95 percent dependent on imports.

Box 1, p. 4:

> The Grain Board (OC) is an SOE created in 1962 under the tutelage of Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources and Fisheries (MAWRF) with a core mandate to regulate and ensure a stable supply of grain on the domestic market through domestic grain harvest collection, imports, and the management of strategic reserves.

> The OC has a de jure monopoly over grain trade (domestic collection and imports), except for barley (animal feed) for which domestic collection (traditionally) and imports (since April 2023) have been authorized for selected private operators.

> The OC buys grain domestically at farmgate prices fixed annually by a government decree. These prices have been below import-parity prices; they were increased by around 60 percent since 2022 to incentivize production.

> The OC sells the grain it purchases at subsidized prices to the millers who are granted specific acquisition quotas; the millers in turn sell the milled products (soft wheat bread flour, soft wheat pastry flour, durum semolina) to bakeries and processors similarly at subsidized prices under quota assignments. End products (such as bread, pasta, and couscous) are sold to consumers at subsidized prices.

> Because of CGC protracted payments, OC must resort to financing by the National Agriculture Bank which is difficult to mobilize and costly.

> CGC, a state-owned entity created in 1970, is responsible for providing compensatory payments to operators at the different segments of the grain value chain to cover the gap between market and administered prices.

Footnote 3:

> Farmgate gate prices in 2023 have been increased by 60.9 percent, 64.2 percent and 60.7 percent for durum wheat, soft wheat and barley respectively, compared to 2021. In February 2024, official farmgate prices for durum wheat and barley are respectively 3 percent sand 14 percent lower than OC import cost (Source OC).

Box 1 continued, p. 5:

> (iii) there are illegal and improper use of subsidized grain products, i.e., improper use of semolina for feed to animals, illegal leakages of grain products towards neighboring countries, as well as excessive consumption and wastage of bread and wheat-based products by end-consumers, e.g., wastage of 900,000 "baguettes" daily; and (iv) the system limits the active participation of the private sector

Para 10, p. 5:

> For calendar years 2022 and 2023, the OC was supposed to receive TND6,625 million (Tunisian Dinar) – i.e., approximately US$2,106 million - from the CGC, but funding effectively received from the compensation fund was only 38 percent (i.e., TND2,543 million or US$808 million).

> As of February 2024, the OC's estimated overall 2023 balance (yet to be audited) amounts to TND -900 million (equivalent to US$ -286 million) and OC's total debt to commercial banks is TND6,343 million (equivalent to US$2,016 million, out of which 83 percent towards the National Agriculture Bank - BNA).

Para 11, p. 5:

> the GoT is carrying out a series of measures that, if fully implemented, would lead to a more sustainable sector and sizeable budget savings in the range of US$400-600 million per year.

Para 10, p. 5 (continued):

> This situation makes it very difficult for OC to access additional financing from commercial banks for grain imports

Para 13:

> This series of reforms would lead to OC's budget and fiscal savings estimated at US$576 million per year

Table 3, "Summary reform measures of the grain value chain and associated savings", measure names (rows extracted as text; fiscal columns not used):

> 4 Strengthening of compensation for losses (FIDAC) [...] Approved (2024 Fiscal Law)- December 31, 2023
> 5 Improved access to seasonal credit for grain producers [...] Approved (2024 Fiscal Law)- December 31, 2023
> 9 Liberalization of soft wheat imports for industrial processing of pastry flour (PS-7) [...] Planned: Cabinet Council to review the draft Decision

Footnote 4 (to Table 3 measure "Strengthening of compensation for losses (FIDAC)", approved in the 2024 Fiscal Law):

> FIDAC (Fonds d'Indemnisation des Dommages Agricoles causés par les Calamités naturelles): is a farmers' compensation fund in case of natural disaster, including drought.

Results framework, p. 43:

> Food subsidy reform implementation plan prepared [...] Preparation of a reform plan for food subsidies and switch to cash transfer, including consultation and communication.

Footnote 17:

> 43.3 percent of bread subsidy for "Gros pain" and 43.5 percent of subsidy for other staple durum wheat-based products go to the poorest two quintiles of Tunisia households in 2022.
resolvedSources.notes: Donor project document; figures on OC finances are sourced to the OC itself and are unaudited. Table 1 rows extracted cleanly; Table 2 (financing gap) extracted with shifted columns and is not used except for its footnote. Table 3 lists nine reform measures (barley import liberalisation April 2023, farmgate price increases, PS-7 flour taxation, planned soft wheat import liberalisation for pastry flour) — recorded as phase 2 leads only.

> AG_FOOD_WST_PC "Food waste per capita (KG)" 2019 | Food Waste Sector HHS | 88.33755 | footnotes ["Very Low Confidence"] | Nature E | source "Food Waste Index Report 2021"
> AG_FOOD_WST_PC 2019 | RTL | 15.17993 | ["Very Low Confidence"] | Food Waste Index Report 2021
> AG_FOOD_WST_PC 2019 | OOHC | 26.83439 | ["Very Low Confidence"] | Food Waste Index Report 2021

> AG_FOOD_WST_PC 2022 | HHS | 171.72145 | ["Medium Confidence"] | Nature E | Food Waste Index Report 2024
> AG_FOOD_WST_PC 2022 | RTL | 9.68092 | ["Very Low Confidence"] | Food Waste Index Report 2024
> AG_FOOD_WST_PC 2022 | OOHC | 31.14722 | ["Very Low Confidence"] | Food Waste Index Report 2024
> AG_FOOD_WST_PC 2022 | ALL | 212.54959 | ["Medium Confidence"] | Food Waste Index Report 2024
> AG_FOOD_WST "Food waste (Tonnes)" 2019 | HHS | 1064406.915 | ["Very Low Confidence"] | Food Waste Index Report 2021
> AG_FOOD_WST 2019 | ALL | 1570650.634 | ["Very Low Confidence"] | Food Waste Index Report 2021
> AG_FOOD_WST 2022 | HHS | 2121810.3 | ["Medium Confidence"] | Food Waste Index Report 2024
> AG_FOOD_WST 2022 | ALL | 2626287.596 | ["Medium Confidence"] | Food Waste Index Report 2024

Attribute codes from the same API (Series/AG_FOOD_WST_PC/Attributes): Nature "E" = "Estimated data".

English gloss: Sectors are HHS = households, RTL = retail, OOHC = out-of-home consumption (food service). Household food waste in Tunisia is estimated at 88 kg per person (2019, Food Waste Index 2021, very low confidence) and 172 kg per person (2022, Food Waste Index 2024, medium confidence), i.e. 1.06 and 2.12 million tonnes.

Search for indicator 12.3.1(a) Food Loss Index (series AG_FLS_PCT) for Tunisia returned totalElements 0.
resolvedSources.notes:
- Food waste here includes inedible parts (bones, peels), per the UNEP definition. It is not comparable with "edible bread thrown away" figures.
- The 2019 and 2022 values come from two editions with different methods and confidence classes. The jump from 88 to 172 kg is not a trend. The change from "Very Low" to "Medium" confidence suggests the 2024 edition used at least one measured data point for Tunisia or a nearby country, but the UNEP report PDF itself (wedocs.unep.org) was behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be opened to check which study.
- No Food Loss Index (12.3.1a) value exists for Tunisia in the database.

resolvedSources.title: Analyse de la filière céréalière en Tunisie et identification des principaux points de dysfonctionnement à l'origine des pertes (Version finale), projet GCP/RNE/004/ITA
resolvedSources.publisher: FAO / Ministère de l'Agriculture (MARHP), authors R. Khaldi and B. Saaidia; hosted by ONAGRI
resolvedSources.extracts:
PDF p. 7 (Contexte de l'étude):

> Dans la région du Proche-Orient et de l'Afrique du Nord, les pertes et gaspillages au niveau de la filière céréalière sont estimés par la FAO à 19 %. Une étude récente, réalisée par l'INC en Tunisie, portant sur le gaspillage du pain, a montré que 900.000 unités de pain sont gaspillées par jour, soit une valeur 100 millions de dinars ($50 million) par an.

> l'importation de plus de 80% des besoins en blé tendre, soit 4 baguettes sur 5 sont importées !

English gloss: FAO estimates cereal-chain losses and waste in the Near East and North Africa at 19% (regional, not Tunisian). A recent INC study found 900,000 bread units wasted per day, worth 100 million dinars a year. Over 80% of soft wheat needs are imported.

PDF p. 12 and p. 34 (Résumé; Collecte):

> La collecte représente, selon les années, entre 40 et 50% de la récolte

English gloss: Collection represents 40-50% of the harvest depending on the year.

PDF p. 56 (Régulation à travers la CGC):

> Il reçoit à cette fin des fonds de la CGC qui permettent de subventionner des opérations de « vente à perte » en raison du décalage entre les prix perçus et les coûts réels. Ainsi, la plus grande partie des frais de logistique et de stockage des céréales est à la charge de l'État.

PDF p. 57:

> En 2007, les charges de compensation ont connu une forte hausse pour les céréales s'élevant à 472 millions de dinars contre 239,5 millions de dinars en 2006

> Les subventions des prix des céréales ont plafonné depuis 2007, atteignant en 2015 une part de 85% du total des charges de compensation des produits alimentaires (tableau 11).

Tableau 11 rows (subsidised quantities): "Blé tendre (million Qx) 10.96 11.2 11.3 11.4 11.726 11.596" for 2011-2016.

Tableau 11 (cereal subsidy amount, million dinars): 2011 887.397; 2012 1010.499; 2013 1134.295; 2014 1166.411; 2015 1392.159; 2016 1286.323.

English gloss: The Office des Céréales receives CGC funds to cover "sales at a loss"; most grain logistics and storage costs are borne by the state. Cereal compensation rose to 472 MD in 2007 from 239.5 MD in 2006 and reached 85% of food compensation in 2015.

PDF p. 61-62 (SWOT, transformation):

> Des produits sont offerts bien en dessous de leur prix de revient, ce qui incite au gaspillage.

> Il existe énormément de gaspillage au niveau de la consommation du pain, qui pourrait avoir plusieurs causes comme la qualité de la matière première (farine), les procédés de fabrication du pain au niveau

English gloss: Products are sold well below cost, which encourages waste. There is a great deal of bread waste at consumption, which could have several causes such as flour quality and bakery processes.

PDF p. 70 (Pertes à la récolte):

> En Tunisie, la récolte mécanique des céréales est malheureusement réputée pour les importantes pertes qu'elle occasionne. Pour donner un exemple, si les pertes sont de l'ordre de 10%, sur une année moyenne (17 millions de quintaux), le volume total des pertes serait de 1,7millions de quintaux.

> En Tunisie, 60% des machines agricoles sont âgées de plus de 25 ans, ce qui occasionne une perte de 100 millions de dinars par an (MARH, 2017).

English gloss: Mechanical harvesting is known for large losses; the 10% figure is a hypothetical example, not a measurement. 60% of farm machines are over 25 years old, causing a loss of 100 MD a year (citing the ministry, 2017).

PDF p. 71-72 (Stockage à la ferme; Collecte):

> Cette différence comprend vraisemblablement des pertes qu'il est très difficile de quantifier chez les agriculteurs.

> La fréquence du stockage en plein air ou dans des silos australiens sans respect des conditions minimales de stockage dont notamment une couverture adéquat du stock,

> L'utilisation quasi-totale des sacs plastiques abimables facilement lors des manutentions

> Lorsque la capacité de stockage est insuffisante ou en année pluvieuse accompagnée d'une bonne récolte, une augmentation du stockage ponctuel à l'air libre est souvent préconisée. Cette pratique peut être à l'origine de pertes importantes : prédateurs, consommation par les oiseaux, retrait de produits impropres lors d'épisodes pluvieux, ou même vols.

English gloss: The gap between harvest and collection probably contains losses that are very hard to quantify on farms. Collection centres often store grain in the open or in uncovered bunker ("Australian") silos, use fragile plastic sacks, and resort to open-air storage in big harvest years, causing losses to pests, birds, rain and theft.

PDF p. 61 (SWOT, première transformation):

> L'OC ne rémunère pas le stockage lorsqu'il est assuré par les minotiers : Ces derniers n'investissent pas suffisamment dans les silos de stockage.

English gloss: The Office des Céréales does not pay millers for storage, so they under-invest in silos.

PDF p. 72 (Stockage à la ferme; Collecte):

> Ce mode de stockage est adopté par les agriculteurs qui souhaitent vendre progressivement leurs céréales sur le marché ou attendre un acheteur. Toutefois, ces derniers ne sont pas encadrés, ni formés sur les bonnes pratiques du stockage.

> L'entrée des privés à la sphère de la collecte reste ponctuelle et ressemble surtout à une sous-traitance plutôt qu'une véritable privatisation de l'activité.

English gloss: Farmers who store grain to sell gradually are neither supported nor trained in good storage practice. Private entry into collection looks like sub-contracting rather than real privatisation.

PDF p. 94 (Conclusion, Bizerte and Siliana):

> on relève l'absence de coordination entre les agriculteurs et les centres de collecte liée à plusieurs facteurs pouvant être à l'origine des pertes : - Pratique de contractualisation peu développée - Faible pouvoir de négociation des agriculteurs, notamment en ce qui concerne les services rendus par les propriétaires de matériel de récolte - Dominance de la petite agriculture à faible accès aux services d'appui technique et financier et peu organisée - Présence d'un circuit parallèle formé par des intermédiaires et d'un circuit informel

English gloss: In Bizerte and Siliana, there is no coordination between farmers and collection centres: little contracting, weak bargaining power of farmers over harvest-machinery owners, predominance of small poorly supported farms, and a parallel circuit of intermediaries and informal trade.

PDF p. 94 (Conclusion):

> A ce jour, peu de données existent en Tunisie sur l'ampleur des pertes aux différents stades de la filière céréalière et peu de pratiques et organisations sont mises en oeuvre pour limiter ces pertes

English gloss: To date, few data exist in Tunisia on the scale of losses at the different stages of the cereal chain.
resolvedSources.notes:
- Phase 1 (diagnostic) report of the FAO/Italy project. It states that loss quantification is the subject of a second phase; that phase 2 report (Bizerte and Siliana estimates) was not found online.
- No date printed on the cover; the latest data cited are from August 2017 and the 2017 investment code decrees, so it is dated 2017 here (possibly finalised in 2018).
- The 18% and 27% cumulative loss figures on PDF p. 67-68 describe France (ADEME / INCOME Consulting 2016), not Tunisia, and are not used.

resolvedSources.title: Évaluation du programme pays de la FAO en Tunisie 2016-2020 (Série évaluation de programme par pays 01/2021)
resolvedSources.extracts:
Annex list of results:

> Réduction des pertes et du gaspillage: Estimation pour la première fois des pertes et gaspillages dans les deux filières stratégiques (céréales et lait) et formation sur la méthodologie de calcul; élaboration des plans d'actions nationaux de réduction des pertes avec une forte implication du Groupement interprofessionnel du lait et la coopérative centrale du blé; appui à l'élaboration des chartes de réduction des pertes et du gaspillage dans les deux filières.

Paragraph 144:

> Le projet GCP/RNE/004/ITA «Réduction des pertes et gaspillage alimentaires et développement des chaînes de valeur pour la sécurité alimentaire en Égypte et en Tunisie» représente une intervention isolée par rapport aux grands axes du CPP. Cette action a néanmoins été assez bien valorisée. Ainsi, il est prévu d'intégrer la mesure des pertes agricoles dans les enquêtes statistiques annuelles du MARHP. L'acquisition d'une expertise dans la mesure des gaspillages par l'Institut national de la consommation est aussi un gage de valorisation de ces acquis.

English gloss: The FAO/Italy project produced the first-ever estimates of losses and waste in the cereal and milk chains, national action plans and loss-reduction charters with the milk interprofession and the central wheat cooperative. It was an isolated intervention; it was planned to integrate the measurement of agricultural losses into the ministry's annual statistical surveys.
resolvedSources.notes: Confirms that before ca. 2017-2018 Tunisia had no chain-level loss estimate for cereals or milk. Whether loss measurement was actually added to the ministry's annual surveys was not verified.

resolvedSources.title: Assessment of the Effect of Climate Change on Wheat Storage in Northwestern Tunisia: Control of Rhyzopertha dominica by Aeration
resolvedSources.publisher: Agronomy 13(7):1773, MDPI (El Melki M.N., Al-Khayri J.M., Aldaej M.I., Almaghasla M.I., El Moueddeb K., Khlifi S.)
resolvedSources.extracts:
Abstract (retrieved from the Crossref and DOAJ metadata APIs for DOI 10.3390/agronomy13071773):

> To project future climate conditions for the period 2041–2070, two climate models, namely MPI-ESM1.2 and CNRMCM5.1, were used under two representative concentration pathways (RCP4.5 and RCP8.5). The study examined the historical and projected feasibility of aeration in six natural regions located in northwestern Tunisia, where wheat is the main crop

> The results revealed a decline in favorable aeration hours due to climate change, resulting in an average reduction of 25% across the six regions. This reduction in aerated hours could significantly affect the effectiveness of aeration as a means of pest control.

> The model predicts a (i) 10–15% extension in the development duration, (ii) 20–30% decrease in reproduction, and (iii) 5–10% decrease in survival relative to the historical period.

English gloss: For 2041-2070 (RCP4.5 and RCP8.5), hours suitable for cooling stored wheat by ambient-air aeration fall by 25% on average in six north-western regions, weakening a key pest-control method; but the modelled lesser grain borer develops more slowly, reproduces 20-30% less and survives 5-10% less than in 1970-1997.
resolvedSources.notes:
- Only the abstract was read: mdpi.com and doaj.org returned HTTP 403 to automated fetches. Full text not checked.
- The paper does not quantify grain losses. Its two results point in opposite directions (less effective aeration vs a less prolific pest), so it does not support a claim that storage losses will rise.

resolvedSources.title: Maîtriser le gaspillage pour assurer la sécurité alimentaire et réduire la faim
resolvedSources.extracts:
Article of 22 November 2018, figures attributed to studies by FAO, INC and the Ministry of Agriculture:

> Les taux moyens de pertes au niveau des exploitations céréalières varient de 4,6% pour le gouvernorat de Bizerte à 7,3% pour le gouvernorat de Siliana. A la collecte, elles sont de 0,38% et 0,24% respectivement.

> Le taux de pertes de lait à la ferme est de 1,96% au gouvernorat de Bizerte et 0,73% à Mahdia. Au transport, les pertes équivalent à 34 litres par transporteurs par jour à Mahdia et 18 litres à Bizerte. Aux centres de collecte, les taux varient de 2,28% à 1,81% respectivement. A la transformation, ils sont en moyenne de 3,5% pour les deux gouvernorats.

> Le manque à gagner par céréaliculteur serait en moyenne de 832,193 DT à Bizerte et 577,803 DT à Siliana.

> Les Tunisiens jettent plus de 113 mille tonnes de pain chaque année, soit 42 kg/ménage/an.

English gloss: Average losses on cereal farms range from 4.6% (Bizerte) to 7.3% (Siliana); at collection 0.38% and 0.24%. Milk losses: 1.96% on farm in Bizerte, 0.73% in Mahdia; collection centres 2.28% and 1.81%; processing 3.5%. Shortfall per cereal farmer: 832 DT in Bizerte, 578 DT in Siliana.
resolvedSources.notes:
- Press summary of the FAO/MARHP/INC phase 2 loss estimates; the cereal loss report itself was not found online.
- Disagrees with SRC-TG-909, which gives 3.6% (Bizerte) to 5.4% (Siliana) "post-récolte" for the same study. The two may measure different scopes (farm stage vs whole post-harvest), but neither article says so.
- The milk collection-centre rates (2.28% Bizerte, 1.81% Mahdia) match the FAO report's collection-centre sub-stage (Tableau 12, SRC-TG-902); the report's "Collecte" stage of 4.38% / 2.65% adds transport losses (2.10% / 0.84%).

resolvedSources.title: Gaspillage alimentaire : des pertes annuelles de 570 millions de dinars
resolvedSources.extracts:
Article of 13 December 2018:

> Lors de sa présence à une conférence régionale organisée récemment par la FAO, le ministre du Commerce, Omar El Béhi, a fait savoir que le gaspillage alimentaire provoque annuellement des pertes excédant 570 millions de dinars.

> En 2017, une étude réalisée conjointement par la FAO, le ministère de l'Agriculture et les Ressources Hydrauliques et l'Institut national de la consommation (INC) a estimé le gaspillage alimentaire- au niveau des restaurants universitaires- à une moyenne de 6% des plats jetés.

> Les taux de pertes post-récolte des céréales varient en moyenne de 3,6% dans la région de Bizerte à 5,4% au niveau de Siliana. Pour la chaîne de valeur lait, les taux de perte sont en moyenne de 9% à Bizerte et 6.5% à Mahdia.

> Le projet lancé en 2016 a entamé en 2018 une deuxième phase portant sur le renforcement des capacités des gestionnaires de restaurants universitaires, des boulangers et des enseignants d'écoles et sur la sensibilisation des élèves et des femmes, notamment les femmes rurales.

English gloss: The Minister of Trade said food waste causes losses exceeding 570 MD a year. A 2017 FAO/ministry/INC study put waste in university canteens at 6% of dishes. Post-harvest cereal losses average 3.6% in Bizerte to 5.4% in Siliana; milk chain losses average 9% in Bizerte and 6.5% in Mahdia. The project started in 2016 and began a second phase in 2018.
resolvedSources.notes:
- Press, tier C. The university canteen figure (6%) conflicts with the 11% given by INC via TAP the month before (SRC-TG-907).
- The cereal rates conflict with SRC-TG-908 (4.6% to 7.3% at farm level).
